features.name: Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserve
features.boundary_scope_note: The statutory preserve includes Card Sound and natural waterways tidally connected to Biscayne Bay, extends across mouths of artificial waterways, and excludes submerged lands conveyed for Biscayne National Monument. FDEP's official GIS layer returns the distinct feature named Biscayne Bay (OBJECTID 43; 64,607.58 acres). Its polygon is an approximate mapped representation, not a legal survey or enforcement boundary.

features.name: Biscayne Bay
features.boundary_scope_note: This is the ecological waterbody entity, distinct from the statutory aquatic preserve and Biscayne National Park boundary. Its complete polygon must be assembled from authoritative shoreline, hydrographic, and tidal-connection evidence. NOAA Harbour ENC chart fragments are preserved individually and are not a complete ecological or statutory boundary. NOAA NGS projects FL1808A-TB-N / GC12021 and FL1808C-TB-N / GC12023 have now been retrieved and their MHW linework inspected. Their 17.691 km nearest-feature separation is diagonal across the bay between opposite-side shoreline features, not an alongshore gap measurement. The project linework does not justify bridging or interpolation. FL1603A provides local Convoy Point comparison only. FDEP preserve geometry remains a separate management overlay. features.name: Biscayne Flats
features.boundary_scope_note: NOAA Harbour ENC names three polygons Biscayne Flats and classifies them as mud flats. This is a charted feature classification, not evidence of current substrate condition, seagrass, fish use, or ecological suitability. The polygons span two ENC cells and require topology review before being assembled into one complex. A first geometric topology precheck found one connected component and no material overlaps. Source polygons remain separate; the charted mud-flat class does not establish current substrate or habitat. The 2005-2013 FWC/NPS unified benthic overlay found 35 discontinuous-seagrass polygons, 17 unconsolidated-sediment polygons, one continuous-seagrass polygon, and one artificial feature intersecting the three old chart polygons; no source polygons were classified as Tidal Flats. The chart name/class and later mapped benthic classes are distinct source concepts.

features.name: Safety Valve
features.boundary_scope_note: NOAA describes a broad area of grass flats and tidal channels near the center of the bay that exchanges water with the Atlantic. It must not be reduced to a single point or a single flat polygon. NOAA ENC names four source polygons as Safety Valve. The source class is named water area, not flat or channel habitat. Preserve the four source features separately until multi-cell geometry reconciliation. A first geometric topology precheck found one connected component and no material overlaps. Source polygons remain separate; this does not establish ecological connectivity or current habitat.

features.name: Government Cut
features.boundary_scope_note: The existing config/places.json point and display radius are approximate and are not an inlet polygon or channel centerline. NOAA Harbour ENC extraction did not return a structured named-water polygon for Government Cut. The Miami Harbor Channel fairway includes nearby dredged/maintained features, but no segment is assigned to Government Cut until a chart-feature crosswalk is completed. NOAA Harbour layer 208 adds three named Miami Harbor Channel fairway polygons (OBJECTIDs 42416, 42420, 42422) across three ENC cells. These remain broader project-channel context; no polygon is assigned to Government Cut.

provenance.title: NOAA ENC GIS Data and Services
NOAA Harbour ENC Fairway Areas, Miami Harbor Channel

features.name: Miami Harbor Channel fairway
features.boundary_scope_note: NOAA ENC Direct to GIS returned 44 maintained-channel features with FAIRWAY='Miami Harbor Channel' across five ENC cells. Features have distinct object names including Cut-1 through Cut-4, Fisher Island Turning Basin, Fishermans Channel, Dodge Island Cut, and Miami Harbor Channel. These must remain distinct source features. The fairway grouping does not identify every segment as Government Cut. A separate Harbour Fairway_area layer (208) returns three named Miami Harbor Channel polygons across three ENC cells; these are not a direct Government Cut subgeometry.

provenance.title: Coastal Maintained Channels, NOAA ENC Direct to GIS
NOAA Harbour ENC Fairway Areas, Miami Harbor Channel

features.name: Norris Cut
features.boundary_scope_note: NOAA Coast Pilot 4, Chapter 11, paragraph 38 describes Norris Cut as a shallow inlet just south of the Main Channel to Miami Harbor between Fisher Island and Virginia Key. NOAA Harbour ENC layer 237 directly returns a named-water polygon for Norris Cut (OBJECTID 253447, Chart 11468, source date 2004-01). This is a charted named-water area, not a surveyed channel centerline or current controlling-depth boundary. The Norris Cut source polygon is persisted in the curated GeoJSON and passed geometry validation. The full inlet channel centerline and current controlling-depth boundary remain unverified.
